records.title: A synthetic approach to Markov kernels, conditional independence and theorems on sufficient statistics
records.sourceVersion: Author arXiv 1908.07021, 98pp; published Advances in Mathematics volume 370 article 107239, 2020

originalEquationLocators.math: Statistical model p:Θ→X, statistic s:X→V a deterministic morphism
originalEquationLocators.meaning: An observation map s must be specified, independent of researcher's physical interpretation.

originalEquationLocators.math: s is sufficient for p iff exists α:V→X such that joint law (parameter Θ, sample X) is reproduced by α applied to statistical observation s(X)
originalEquationLocators.meaning: Exact common reconstruction map α is part of structural equivalence; not just matching scalar entropy.

records.actualDynamics: Probabilistic category and sufficient-statistic representation; not a general source dynamics/generative physical rule.
criticalAssumptions: Monoidal copy/delete structural axioms of Markov category
Deterministic statistic morphism s and Markov models
Some results require strictly positive Markov category and disintegrations
records.structuralRelevance: A precise abstract equivalence contract for recovering named source transitions/outcomes from coarse observer; T3's classical conditional KL test is a special finite-statistical analogy.
records.exactObstruction: No native global probability kernel, dimension or measure uniquely derived; do not assign quantum/physical status to abstract Markov arrows.
records.evidenceStatus: original PDF p84 Defs14.2–14.3 visually inspected; no proof recapitulated

records.title: Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro
records.sourceVersion: Original open PNAS 110(49):19790–19795 published December 2013; full source text including definition and methodological discussion read.

originalEquationLocators.where: PNAS original Main Text section State-Independent Causal Analysis
originalEquationLocators.math: EI(S)=MI(U^C;U^E) under uniformly perturbed possible cause repertoire U^C and transition probability matrix defining effect repertoire U^E
originalEquationLocators.meaning: Effective information refers to imposed intervention distribution and source transition kernel; not generic intrinsic microcausal completeness.

originalEquationLocators.where: PNAS original Micro Macro Mappings and Repertoires of Alternatives
originalEquationLocators.math: Under macro coarsening, impose a separate uniform macro intervention distribution, which changes underlying micro-state perturbation weights
originalEquationLocators.meaning: A macro effective-information increase need not violate classical data processing under a single fixed input ensemble because the intervention ensemble changed.

objects: intervention distribution fixed uniform at each scale
records.actualDynamics: Specified transitions with macro/micro intervention-based information measures; not a new physical force or spacetime emergence.
criticalAssumptions: Discrete state repertoire and transition probability matrix
Uniform interventions chosen anew at each tested scale
records.structuralRelevance: Direct adversarial control for interpreting a high macro-information score as a new physical causal structure; compare under identical transported intervention distributions too.
records.exactObstruction: No guarantee a macro model recovers all source-native legal rewrites even when its normalized effective information exceeds micro under a rescaled intervention prior.
records.evidenceStatus: original open full journal HTML section read; some displayed main-text mathematical symbols rendered as figures, method interpretation verified in prose

records.title: Sufficient Subalgebras and the Relative Entropy of States of a von Neumann Algebra
records.sourceVersion: Communications in Mathematical Physics 105, 123–131 (1986), author's archived original 10pp

originalEquationLocators.math: S(φ,ω)=S(φ|M0,ω|M0) (weak sufficiency); for finite S and faithful state, equivalent to [Dφ,Dω]_t∈M0 for every t
originalEquationLocators.meaning: A subalgebra observation sufficient for a pair of quantum states preserves relative entropy and specific Radon–Nikodym cocycle.

originalEquationLocators.math: Equivalent to existence of sufficient subalgebra and preserving conditional expectation conditions under theorem's hypotheses
originalEquationLocators.meaning: Exact recovery/sufficiency is stronger than matching any one entropy-like scalar outside assumptions.

objects: von Neumann algebra M with subalgebra M0
faithful normal states φ and ω
records.actualDynamics: No microscopic dynamical rewrite specified; this is a theorem characterizing quantum statistical observations and recoverability.
criticalAssumptions: modular theory and conditional expectation definitions
not a classical hypergraph transformation theorem
records.structuralRelevance: Formal source for a quantum information recoverability notion, but our native simulator currently supports only source event occurrence and binary bits.
records.exactObstruction: Classical T3 KL-chain equality under a chosen probability model is only an analogy and does not construct von Neumann algebra quantum Petz sufficiency.
records.evidenceStatus: original PDF p1 and Theorem4 PDF p5 visually inspected; proof not reproduced

importantNewContrast: Causal emergence EI comparison reweights uniform interventions separately at each grain; do not misuse its macro>micro result as data processing violation under one fixed ensemble.
